_note: Verified against real on-device Trust Wallet Core 4.1.19 (the pinned version on both platforms), via the Android instrumented test AddressDerivationConformanceTest.kt, run 2026-08-27 on an emulator. Independently cross-checked with the WASM build (@trustwallet/wallet-core 3.3.3, run standalone in Node) as a second data point — the two agree on all chains except ton (see that entry's _note); on-device 4.1.19 is authoritative on any disagreement, since that's what the app actually ships. Test mnemonic is the BIP39 standard test vector — never use with real funds. This pass verified Android only: no Swift/Xcode toolchain was available to run the equivalent check on iOS (ChainKey.coinType maps identically on both platforms, so the derivation itself should match, but that has not been independently confirmed on-device for iOS — see README.md's Security model section). See conformance/signing-vectors.json for byte-for-byte signed-output vectors.

The WASM cross-check (@trustwallet/wallet-core 3.3.3) derives the identical underlying public-key hash but defaults to the bounceable (EQ...) address-flag encoding instead (EQAzWZa6nM5mJev91wGc7VCSfBoIsYRqKJpV78N8Add9-U9d) — a version/binding difference in default address flags, not a key-derivation discrepancy. On-device 4.1.19 is authoritative since that's what the app actually ships; worth being aware of if this fixture is ever cross-checked again with a newer/different wallet-core binding.
